headline: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie has signed a 45-day pause on new data centre development across the city.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a signed citywide moratorium in a major US tech city, but it lasts only 45 days and the rules that follow are not yet written.
importance_line: San Francisco residents and data centre developers face a 45-day pause while the city studies the effects and drafts controls, and the city will also learn how many data centres it has, which its Planning Department did not know.
summary: The San Francisco Standard reports that Mayor Daniel Lurie signed on 16 Oct 2026 a moratorium, written by Supervisor Shamann Walton, that pauses new data centre development citywide for 45 days, after the Board of Supervisors approved it unanimously the week before, a vote our 7 Oct 2026 edition reported. During the pause the Planning Department is to study the impacts of data centres and develop controls, and the Standard notes that the department did not know how many data centres exist in the city, where at least six are counted.
notes: Read in full. The moratorium would have taken effect without his signature; Lurie's statement did not mention data centres explicitly. Board vote was the previous week (date not stated).
